rounds.proof_sketch: Input dtype is fixed at torch.float32. AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES instantiates scalar_t=float. The mutation removes (float) cast from val1 where val1 is already float. Casting float→float is a no-op, so fabsf((float)val1) ≡ fabsf(val1) for all float values. Even for double inputs, fabsf() implicitly converts double→float identically to the explicit cast.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation removes an explicit (float) cast from val1 before passing it to fabsf(). Since the input tensor has dtype=torch.float32 (fixed by contract), the template parameter scalar_t is instantiated as float. When scalar_t=float, val1 is already of type float, making the (float) cast a no-op. The fabsf() function signature is float fabsf(float), so passing a float directly is semantically identical to casting a float to float first. Layer 2 testing confirmed bitwise identical results across 112 rounds including extreme values, near-zero, sparse, and boundary cases.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. The mutation removes a redundant type cast from float to float. The only way to potentially expose a difference would be to change the input dtype to float64, which is prohibited by the testing contract. Even with float64 inputs, the implicit conversion in fabsf(double_val) produces identical results to the explicit cast (float)double_val.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing tools should recognize that removing explicit casts between identical types (e.g., (float) on a float variable) creates equivalent mutants. A static analysis pass detecting self-casts would prevent these equivalent mutants from being generated in the first place.
